name: create-omits-defaulted-time
expect: 201 — fecha carries default:"now", injected by the engine. THE regression pin: the 2026-08-01 create type check rejected the engine's own time.Time and broke every POST omitting the field, with make test green

name: create-decimal-to-int
expect: 422 validation_failed fields[amount rule=type] — the silent-truncation corruption (stored 1, answered 201) closed by ADR-024

name: create-string-scalar-int
expect: 201 — a JSON string defers to Postgres on create (form-encoded clients); refusing it was the adversarial review's first catch

name: create-bool-to-int
expect: 422 fields[amount rule=type] — used to be a masked 500

name: create-noninitial-state
expect: 422 — a row may only be created in an initial state (G5)

name: create-enum-invalid
expect: 422 — enum violation, S44 shape

name: create-unique-collision
expect: 409 — unique collision on code (seeded C1), masked PG error never exposed

name: create-missing-required
expect: 422 fields[title rule=required]

name: update-decimal-to-int
expect: ENG-29: 422 validation_failed fields[amount rule=type] — was the flat {"error":"field \"amount\" must be an integer"}; create and update now answer one shape

name: update-unknown-field
expect: ENG-29: 422 fields[ghost rule=unknown_field] — was a flat string

name: update-sets-id
expect: ENG-29: 422 fields[id rule=read_only] — was a flat string

name: update-auto-field
expect: fecha is NOT auto (it has a default) so this is a legal write — 200 on both; pins that default fields stay writable

name: update-bad-uuid-value
expect: ENG-29 shape: 422 fields[ref rule=type] — was flat

name: update-multi-errors-at-once
expect: ENG-29: ALL THREE violations in one 422 fields[] — the flat form reported only the first, in map order

name: update-illegal-transition
expect: 422 invalid transition open→done (state machine, race-safe in the UPDATE WHERE) — unchanged

name: update-empty-body
expect: 400 empty body — unchanged

name: put-missing-required
expect: ENG-29: 422 fields[title rule=required] — was flat missing required field

name: tx-update-decimal-to-int
expect: ENG-29 on the batch path: 422 validation_failed + fields[] naming the op — a batch op is validated exactly like its single-op counterpart

name: tx-forbidden-op
expect: 403 forbidden naming the op — unchanged; deny detail goes to the server log only (ENG-27)

name: filter-wrong-typed-int
expect: ENG-25: 400 naming filter[amount][gt], the value and int64 — was the anonymous {"error":"invalid request"} from the masked PG error

name: filter-overflow-int
expect: ENG-25: 400 named (out of int64 range in every PG version) — was anonymous

name: filter-overflow-float
expect: ENG-25: 400 named — was anonymous

name: filter-bool-yes-still-works
expect: 200 — Postgres accepts yes as boolean; the acceptors reproduce PG's grammar, never Go's (the measured constraint that shaped ENG-25)

name: filter-bool-prefix-t
expect: 200 — PG unique-prefix boolean

name: filter-time-garbage-documented-gap
expect: 400 anonymous on BOTH — time is deliberately excluded from ENG-25 (PG's timestamp grammar is not reproducible safely); the documented exception, visible here

name: filter-jsonb-invalid
expect: ENG-25: 400 naming filter[attrs][eq] and jsonb — was anonymous

name: filter-by-id
expect: ENG-26: 200 with the row — id (the implicit PK) is filterable like sort already allowed; was 400 unknown filter field

name: filter-by-id-bad-value
expect: ENG-26+25: 400 naming the uuid value — was 400 unknown filter field

name: filter-by-id-bad-op
expect: 400 — uuid allows eq only; names the operator and the allowed set

name: filter-unknown-field
expect: 400 available: now truthfully includes id (ENG-26 closed the self-contradiction)

name: filter-op-underscore
expect: 400 naming is_null + allowed set (ENG-14/ADR-024; SCHEMA-6 keeps NULL-filtering an honest dead end)

name: filter-op-capital
expect: 400 — op validated in code, not regex-dropped

name: filter-malformed
expect: 400 malformed filter parameter

name: filter-empty-nontext
expect: 400 empty value is not valid for a int64 field

name: agg-filter-wrong-typed
expect: ENG-25 reached the aggregate FOR FREE (BuildAggregate delegates to BuildQuery) — verified, not assumed (the ENG-14 lesson)

name: agg-filter-by-id
expect: ENG-26 inherited by the aggregate path — 200 count:1

name: page-zero
expect: 400 must be a positive integer (ADR-024 second axis)

name: page-negative
expect: 400 must be a positive integer

name: page-alpha
expect: 400 must be a positive integer — the message that always existed; the code now keeps its promise

name: page-empty
expect: ENG-30: 400 — an empty form field was silently served as page 1 while page=0 was already a named 400; presence is the gate now

name: per-page-empty
expect: ENG-30: 400 named

name: per-page-over-cap
expect: 200 clamped to 100 and REPORTED in meta.per_page — documented tolerance, not silence (ADR-024 §5)

name: sort-empty
expect: ENG-30: 400 naming the empty value + available fields — was silently unsorted

name: sort-unknown
expect: 400 unknown sort field + available list

name: sort-multi
expect: 400 — multi-field sort does not exist and says so

name: order-empty-with-sort
expect: ENG-30: 400 use asc or desc — was silently ASC

name: order-bad-direction
expect: 400 use asc or desc

name: order-without-sort
expect: ENG-30: 400 order requires sort — was read by nothing and dropped

name: keyset-after
expect: 200 keyset page (after the zero uuid = every row, deterministic) — unchanged

name: keyset-discards-sort-open
expect: 200 on BOTH — ENG-15 (cursor silently discards sort, meta.page lies) is OPEN in the backlog; the corpus documents open items too

name: repeated-filter-open
expect: 200 with the C1 row — the FIRST value wins and the correction is dropped (ENG-17, OPEN); if last-wins ever ships this row goes empty and the diff says so

name: search-basic
expect: 200 ILIKE across string fields — unchanged

name: bearer-lowercase
expect: 200 — RFC 9110 auth scheme is case-insensitive and the engine's own OpenAPI advertises "bearer" (ADR-024 F-7)

name: basic-scheme-named
expect: 401 naming the SCHEME, not blaming a token the caller never sent (F-8)

name: no-auth
expect: 401 — unchanged

name: host-uppercase
expect: 200 — RFC 9110 host case-insensitivity (F-7)

name: host-invalid-label
expect: 400 naming the label and the rule, truncated (the DoS-amplifier lesson: echo the label once, max 32 runes)

name: rbac-undeclared-role

name: rbac-declared-denied
expect: 403 {"error":"forbidden"} — must be byte-identical to rbac-undeclared-role (compare the two rows by eye: same body)

name: viewer-field-allowlist
expect: 200 with only id,title,status projected — unchanged
